# dupl

**dupl** is a tool for finding code clones in Go source files.

## Usage

```
Usage of dupl:
  dupl [flags] [paths]

Paths:
  If the given path is a file, dupl will use it regardless of
  the file extension. If it is a directory it will recursively
  search for *.go files in that directory.

  If no path is given dupl will recursively search for *.go
  files in the current directory.

Flags:
  -files
        read file names from stdin one at each line
  -html
        output the results as HTML, including duplicate code fragments
  -plumbing
        plumbing (easy-to-parse) output for consumption by scripts or tools
  -t, -threshold size
        minimum token sequence size as a clone (default 15)
  -vendor
        check files in vendor directory
  -v, -verbose
        explain what is being done

Examples:
  dupl -t 100
        Search clones in the current directory of size at least
        100 tokens.
  dupl $(find app/ -name '*_test.go')
        Search for clones in tests in the app directory.
  find app/ -name '*_test.go' |dupl -files
        The same as above.
```

func filterSubsumed(groups [][]span) [][]span {
	// Build an index from span (file, offset range) to group.
	// For each group, check whether all its spans are covered by another
	// group of strictly larger length.
	sort.SliceStable(groups, func(i, j int) bool {
		return groups[i][0].length > groups[j][0].length
	})
	// Greedy: for each span, track the largest group it belongs to.
	type key struct {
		file string
		off  int
		end  int
	}
	type assignment struct {
		groupIdx int
		length   int
	}
	owner := map[key]assignment{}
	accept := make([]bool, len(groups))
	for gi, grp := range groups {
		// If every span in grp is strictly contained in an already-emitted group, skip.
		allCovered := true
		for _, s := range grp {
			k := key{file: s.file, off: s.offStart, end: s.offEnd}
			_ = k
			if !isContained(owner, s) {
				allCovered = false
				break
			}
		}
		if allCovered {
			continue
		}
		accept[gi] = true
		for _, s := range grp {
			owner[key{file: s.file, off: s.offStart, end: s.offEnd}] = assignment{groupIdx: gi, length: s.length}
		}
	}
	out := make([][]span, 0, len(groups))
	for i, g := range groups {
		if accept[i] {
			out = append(out, g)
		}
	}
	return out
}
